text: Though I could make myself feared, I had yet much rather make myself beloved: there are so many sorts of defects in old age, so much imbecility, and it is so liable to contempt, that the best acquisition a man can make is the kindness and affection of his own family; command and fear are no longer his weapons.
author: Michel de Montaigne
locator: Book II, Chapter 8, Of the Affection of Fathers to their Children
translation: Charles Cotton, ed. W. C. Hazlitt, 1877
